summary: The maze CHECKPOINTS and HAZARDS induce from frames EXACTLY, correcting the earlier 'they draw on the floor / are invisible' conclusion: both leave a static marking that is frame-readable.
key_finding: CHECKPOINTS render as a DITHERED 4x4 checkerboard of the OBJECT's colour (isolated diagonal pixels, fill ~0.5) -- distinct from the SOLID object and the HOLLOW-outline target; found by removing the object+target regions from the object-colour mask then 8-connecting the remaining dither. HAZARDS render a static MARKER in distinct low-area colours in a tight horizontal band; found as the bbox of those marker cells. (The earlier probe sampled the box CENTRE -- floor -- and missed both markings.)
also_fixed: induce_object_target_attrs now PREFERS a notched sprite as the object/target (a notchless solid square is a WALL, not the object) -- this excluded the L7 wall (33,16) that was previously mis-picked as the object. The L1-L5 target-attrs end-to-end is unregressed (5/5 env-confirmed).
circularity_note: Frame-only perception validated against internal-state ground truth; NOT a moat / oracle-distinct claim.
model_specs: frame-only perception (numpy/scipy.ndimage region analysis on grid_of(frame)); no LLM/GPU
closes: the maze-sub-fields portion of GAP-ARC-MAZE-MODEL-FRAME-INDUCTION: object, walls, target, object/target attrs, AND now checkpoints + hazards all induce from frames.
remaining: the full frame-only maze SOLVE (assembling all fields into a planner run) still needs COMPLETE wall geometry from a single frame + move-code induction + the spikes_hidden residual hitbox -- a separate integration step beyond inducing the sub-fields.
